AUTHOR: D. McIntosh; T. P. Marques; A. Branzan Albu; R. Rountree; F. De Leo
TITLE: TempNet: Temporal Attention Towards the Detection of Animal Behaviour in Videos
REGION: Ocean Networks Canada cabled observatory, NE Pacific (British Columbia, Canada)
SPECIES: Sablefish (Anoplopoma fimbria) startle vs no startle
DATA: Sablefish startle clip dataset of McIntosh et al. (ONC observatory video), 892 4-s clips
D_EV: Sec. IV.A: 'This dataset consists of a total of 892 clips... 100 clips are reserved for testing, 150 for validation.'
R_EV: Sec. IV.C: 'All evaluation metrics are generated on the test set of the dataset presented in [14].'
E_EV: Table II: only 'Accuracy Precision BCE False Neg. False Pos. F1' reported for clip-wise startle detection
ARCH: TempNet (3D CNN, temporal attention, residual blocks, wavelet down-sampling); baselines ReMotENet, hybrid YOLOv3+LSTM
METR: accuracy, precision, F1, BCE, FP/FN counts, inference time
NOTE: Clip-level behaviour classification (startle events) on ONC observatory video. Split given only as clip counts drawn from videos with no grouping statement -> coded 이미지/프레임 무작위 per rule (could be argued NR). E4 = FNR because false negative counts reported. Behaviour is the target but only classification metrics reported -> E1 없음. No confidence threshold value reported (sigmoid output) -> C_ALL NR rather than NA. Text is arXiv version of ICPR 2022 paper.
